The text identifies "good versus evil" as the primary shared theme in both J.R.R. Tolkien's 'The Lord of the Rings' and C.S. Lewis's 'The Chronicles of Narnia'.

The similarity lies in the presence of this central moral conflict in both works. However, the presentation of this theme differs significantly. In 'The Lord of the Rings', the theme is presented with a clear distinction between the forces of good and those of darkness, set within a complex world. In contrast, 'The Chronicles of Narnia' presents a more nuanced view by blurring the lines between good and evil, often introducing characters who waver between sides.
